facts.fact: A newly cemented pond releases free lime into the water, and this can harm fish and plants.
Concrete is basic by nature and has to be treated, or it will change the pond water's pH.
The pH of a concrete pond may need adjusting from time to time for some time after it is built.
A dark pigment paint or masonry sealant on the concrete moderates the pond's pH.
The main job of a sealant painted inside a concrete pond is to stop lime in the cement leaching into the water.
One keeper reported that water put into a new cement tank went above pH 10.
Another guide says to soak each fill for 24-48 hours, drain completely, and repeat at least 3 to 5 times.
Scrub all surfaces with a stiff brush, especially the corners and floor, then rinse well so no residue is left.
To take away the cement smell, soak cut banana stems, 2-3 kg of bundled rice straw, or 2-3 chopped pineapples in the pond for 5-7 days. Then remove them and rinse the pond several times.
When soaking banana stems, keep the water at or above the level the pond will hold once fish are in.
Ponds waterproofed with PU, bitumen-based or black paint coatings need a 2-4 week soak, because these coatings can be toxic to fish.
Test pH before adding fish and aim for about neutral (pH 7). Readings higher than that mean the water is too alkaline.
A Vietnamese koi guide gives pH 7-7.5 as the target before stocking a new cement pond, rechecking 24 hours after each adjustment.
If pH is still high, a failed seal is not the only possible cause: wait a few more days and test again.
Chewy's own break-in schedule: fill the new pond for a week, then drain and refill. Repeat after two weeks, after three weeks, and after one more week; the whole break-in takes about 10 weeks.
Chewy: one week after the last refill, test the pond's pH against tap water left out overnight, and look for the two to match within 0.2 units.
Pond Expert's vinegar cure: 1 gallon of household vinegar per 200 gallons of pond water, left for three days, then empty the pond and rinse it thoroughly.
Commercial fish-safe sealers can shorten the curing process.
One keeper sealed a tank with Pond Armor and reported that the water then tested the same as tap water.
Leaving vinegar or cleaning-agent residue in the pond, and not measuring pH, are named as mistakes.
One keeper's vinegar dose dropped pH from above 10 to 4.5, but it was back at 10 after 6 hours. Acid alone did not stop the lime leaching.
A thin layer of fresh cement put over an already waterproofed tank was suspected of causing large pH swings. The keeper chose to recoat it with pond sealer.
Channel catfish fry 7 to 14 days after hatching suffer heavy losses from a sudden pH rise of 0.5.
Stocking fish into ponds with pH above 8.0 can cause deaths. Measure pH in both the transport water and the receiving water when stocking, with a pH pen.
Most finfish species are probably vulnerable to pH shock if stocked 7 to 14 days after hatching.
Vietnamese koi keepers soak banana stems (thân chuối) in a new cement pond to remove the cement smell.
A Vietnamese guide suggests 2-3 dried Indian almond (bàng) leaves as a natural way to adjust pH in a new pond.
